demand.headline: The demonstration hub draws 750 kWh a day for 300 swaps (1,000 kWh if every battery came back empty), and 1,367 kWh at 24 months under base adoption.
demand.how: How this is calculated: kWh a swap = pack kWh × (1 − state of charge on return) ÷ charging efficiency; swaps grow at the adoption case's rate, compounding yearly; charging power = kWh a day ÷ the feeder's hours of supply. Adoption cases are assumptions, not forecasts. Every hub is synthetic.

sites.headline: 4 of 6 hubs fit on the grid now; 2 still fit at 24 months under base adoption.
sites.how: How this is calculated: the DT's observed peak in the month, grown 5% a year, against its rating; the hub's draw (kWh a day ÷ the feeder's hours of supply, at most its chargers) ÷ power factor 0.95, taken at the DT's peak; and whether the chargers can take the day's energy in the feeder's hours. Hours of supply are calculated from the outage log, never read from the band. Synthetic network and hubs.

power.headline: At the demonstration hub, diesel costs ₦1,092.49/kWh in fuel (₦583.33/kWh at the low price) against ₦63.33/kWh on the Band B grid with diesel backup; solar options wait for an EPC quote.
power.how: How this is calculated: each hub at its own feeder's band tariff and hours of supply; diesel ₦3,277.47 a litre (NBS, May 2026), with ₦1,750 (TechCabal, July 2026) as the low case, ÷ 3 kWh a litre (assumption), fuel only; PV sized to the average day at the hub's peak sun hours × 0.80, making up the BESS's 90% round-trip efficiency, so a rainy-season day leaves a shortfall the backup meets; CO2 avoided against petrol vehicles over the same distance, the grid at 0.395 kg a kWh (IFI, 2019 dataset). Synthetic hubs.

finance.headline: ₦165.0 million of the ₦340.0 million pledged is placed on 3 hubs; ₦175.0 million is queued. 2 of the hubs offered need a DT upgrade; 2 wait for the PV and BESS cost.
finance.how: How this is calculated: margin a swap = the ₦3,000 swap price (reported) − the energy cost a swap on the hub's power option (calculated, at the base diesel price) − ₦600 non-energy opex (assumption: 20% of the swap price, for staff, site and battery wear); half the margin (assumption) goes into escrow and repays the hub's funder; months to repay = the hub's cost repaid from escrow at the funder's return. A hub whose margin is 0 or less cannot repay on that power option and no repaid pledge is matched to it. The ₦1,000 deducted from each swap (reported) repays the rider's conversion loan and is never counted as hub revenue. A hub is offered on a power option that works at its site through 24 months: the grid where it fits; the grid after a named DT upgrade where only the DT rating fails; solar + BESS where the feeder's hours of supply fail, its PV and BESS cost added to the hub's. Pledges are placed lowest return first, then fewer feeders, then id; a pledge funds a hub on a feeder it names, when it has the whole cost left and the hub repays within its tenor. Hub costs are synthetic, only to exercise the matching; they are not investment figures.
